description: Retrieval benchmark for the sample dataset. Every expectation names a memory by its exact content, not by a database id: ids are assigned at import time and change on every re-import, so a benchmark keyed on them would silently start testing nothing. The evaluator derives a stable content key on both sides and reports any expectation it cannot resolve.

queries.query: Which database does the user service use for persistence?

expected.content: The user service uses PostgreSQL 15 for persistence.
expected.why: The current decision, stated with the words used in the query.

expected.content: The user service uses MySQL for persistence.
expected.why: The outdated decision. Still relevant: a retriever that only surfaces one of two conflicting memories hides the conflict.

queries.query: Add caching to the user service.

expected.content: We disabled Redis caching for user records because stale cache entries caused wrong account balances.
expected.why: Directly about caching user records; the reason the last attempt was reverted.

expected.content: We removed the in-memory account snapshot because balances could go stale after writes.
expected.why: The same lesson learned a second way, phrased without the word 'caching'. A keyword retriever misses this.

expected.content: We disabled Redis caching for user records because stale cache entries caused wrong account balances.
Redis caching was disabled for user records after stale cache entries produced incorrect account balances.
expected.why: The same decision recorded twice; either wording satisfies the query.

queries.query: Why did account balances go wrong after writes?

expected.content: We removed the in-memory account snapshot because balances could go stale after writes.
We disabled Redis caching for user records because stale cache entries caused wrong account balances.
expected.why: The related earlier incident; same failure mode, different layer.

queries.query: How do we handle duplicate refund events delivered twice by the payment provider?

expected.content: Stripe webhook handlers must be idempotent because Stripe retries deliveries.
expected.why: This is the answer, and it shares no content word with the query. Keyword retrieval scores it zero.

queries.query: Which background job queue do we use?

expected.content: We migrated from Celery to Dramatiq for background jobs in 2025.
Background jobs are queued through Celery with Redis as the broker.
expected.why: The superseded answer. Returning it is correct: the conflict is the useful signal.

queries.query: What Python runtime do the backend services use?

expected.content: Python 3.8 is the runtime for all backend services.
Python 3.11 is the runtime for all backend services.
The reporting service runs on the same PostgreSQL cluster as the user service.
expected.why: The only PostgreSQL memory in this namespace. Matching the payments-api memories here would be a namespace leak.

queries.query: Is it safe to log payment card data?

expected.content: Never log full card numbers or CVV values; use the last four digits only.

queries.query: How do we roll out a Kubernetes helm chart to the cluster?
queries.why: Nothing in this collection covers deployment tooling. A retriever that returns something here is inventing relevance.
